steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Generously grease two 9x5-inch loaf pans.
Melt chocolate squares in a microwave-safe glass or ceramic bowl in 15-second intervals, stirring after each interval, 1 to 3 minutes.

Beat sugar, zucchini, oil, eggs, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer until well combined. Beat in melted chocolate. Stir in flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon until just blended. Fold in chocolate chips. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pans.
Bake loaves in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of each loaf comes out clean, 60 to 70 minutes.
Cool to room temperature before slicing. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Zucchini Bread
raw_recipe.description: This easy chocolate zucchini bread is moist, fudgy, and made with a double dose of chocolate for a delicious way to use up a surplus of zucchini.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Zucchini Bread

review.reviewBody: This bread is really good. I made a few changes, because I know what I like in a quick bread. I like it to be really moist and I find that the recipes with sour cream in them are best acomplished in this way, so I added 1 cup sour cream. I was also concerned with it not being chocolatey enough, so I added a few tablespoons of cocoa to the dry ingredients. I also added extra chocolate chips. I also did what other reviewers suggest, and add the choc chips to the dry ingredients so they don't sink and it worked well. I added a little more zucchini also. And seriously, this is the absolute best bread I've put zucchini into ever! And I've been making different zucchini bread recipes all week. (I have a ton of zucchini in my garden). With the changes I made, I would consider it about perfect! I'll make it again and again. You would never know it had zucchini in it. It's perfectly moist and delicious. Like a rich chocolate cake. Just wonderful!

This bread is a wonderful, chocolatey treat. The texture is very moist. My only suggestions are: 1) thoroughly grease the pans, 2) use mini chocolate chips in the recipe, and 3) let the loaves cool at least 10 minutes before you try to remove them from the pan.

We LOVE this recipe in the Fall. A great comfort treat and a good use of plentiful zucchini. I use the cocoa powder and half the oil and replace with applesauce. I use mini chocolate chips and add a handful of cinnamon chips. I also cut parchment paper to fit the bottom of the pans then coat the inside with cooking spray. I let the bread cool 20 minutes on a wire rack, run a knife around the edges and the bread falls right out. Nothing stuck to the bottom.

This is a delicious recipe that I am sure to make again. I did make the following changes as follows; I followed another reviewer's suggestion to used 6 TBS cocoa powder & 2 TBS oil instead of unsweetened chocolate, and instead of oil, I typically substitute unsweetened applesauce, and it made beautiful, moist muffins in about 24 mins. Don't forget to add 1 cup of walnuts!

I followed the recipe exactly except I didn't have 2oz unsweetened chocolate squares, so I made it with 2T melted shortening and stirred in 6T unsweetened cocoa powder. Needed to melt it anyway per recipe so it was an easy substitution. I read the many reviews that said the bread stuck to the bottom of the pan. I learned a trick recently - spray the pan, cut wax or parchment paper to line the bottom, then spray it as well. Mine came out perfectly. It seems to be more of a cake batter than a bread batter, and the smell has me thinking it needs to be topped with vanilla ice cream. :) My husband is circling the kitchen island wondering when it will be cool enough to cut.
I use 3 Tbs. of Hershey's cocoa powder instead of melting chocolate. I also spray pans with Pam and line the bottom of the pans with parchment paper.

So delicious! I substituted the 2oz chocolate with 6 tbsp cocoa & added 1 teaspoon of baking powder. Greased the pan heavily with butter & the outside came out perfectly crunchy while the inside was moist & light! 
I used one 9x5 inch loaf pan & it fit perfectly. 
Served with whipped cream. 
Will definitely make again!

Excited to bring this one to work - it turned out amazing! I ended up baking 4 loaves and made a few minor adjustments between the two batches. Adjustments made for both batches: - 2.5 cups of zucchini instead of 2 cups - Substituted canola oil for vegetable oil - 6 Tbsps cocoa powder + 2 Tbsps butter instead of the unsweetened chocolate (mix the cocoa with the dry ingredients, melt the butter, and add it in with the wet ingredients) - Added 1.5 tsps vanilla instead of 1 tsp - Mini semi-sweet chocolate chips (I shook them in a cocoa powder + cinnamon mixture). I folded most of them in like the recipe said and then sprinkled the remainder on top. I did not have issues with the chocolate chips sinking to the bottom. - I used crisco for the pans and parchment paper on the bottom. Additional adjustments made for high-altitude (6000 ft+): - I added one extra yolk - Added 2 Tbsps coffee - Added 3 Tbsps of flour - Reduced the sugar by 3 Tbsps - Reduced the baking soda from 1 tsp to 3/4 tsp The first batch I baked at 365 degrees for 52 minutes and took it out a few minutes early. It was a little crisp on the ends, but it's still moist. The second batch I reduced the temperature to 355 degrees and baked two more loaves for 48 minutes. All loaves held their shape well and did not cave in the middle. If I were baking this again, I'd bake it at 355 for and begin checking it around 45 minutes. That said - they all turned out really well and were a huge hit. Definitely recommend!!

This was delicious! I used a forgotten zucchini from my garden, it ended up being closer to 4 cups shredded; other than that, the recipe did the trick. I made one loaf, and 18 muffins (baked for 20-22 minutes). Will definitely make this again!

Amazing! I didn’t have enough vegetable oil so I used coconut oil. Because of this I was worried it might be too sweet so I halved the sugar and I’m glad I did. I also took another person’s recommendation and added 1/2 cup of sour cream to make it more moist and a tbls of cocoa powder for more chocolate flavor. 1 accidentally added 2oz of unsweetened chocolate instead of 1 oz but I went with it and I’m glad I did. It turned out so moist and chocolatey. 

I used two 9x5 loaf pans but the cake only filled about half of each - next time I’ll see if I can fit it all into one loaf pan or make “15 servings” for one loaf. 

Great recipe!

I left out the chocolate and used dark chocolate chips. Yummy. As to the dough sticking to pan, as with most sweet breads, one should line the pan with parchment paper so that you can lift it right out when done baking.
It didn’t come out of the pans easily. Flavor was good.
I think this recipe is perfect and I wouldn’t change a thing. Thank you for sharing it.

Love this! Used coconut oil and a mix of dark and semi chocolate chips. Released better from non-stick pan than my glass pan. Will try mini chips next. 2nd bake: Use mini chips and fine side of grater which made it less crumbly, would go back to adding some dark chips though. will try butter and applesauce next time.
With an overabundance of zucchini I decided to double the recipe. Its so good!
Easy and delicious. The cinnamon adds a nice touch!

This is my favorite zucchini bread. After moving back to the Western slope of Colorado, I did have to make a few modifications since the high altitude changes how things bake. Decreased baking soda by 1/4 tsp., added 3 tablespoons of water, decreased sugar about 3 tablespoons as well. Increased temp to 375°. I also throughly sprayed the pans, lined with parchment paper, sprayed the paper and dusted with cocoa powder instead of flour since it's a chocolate quick bread. Also, to keep the chocolate chips from sinking, I shook them in a ziplock with some cocoa powder. Oh, and if you butter your slices, fry on the stove just a bit and dollop cool whip or ice cream on it, it makes a fabulous dessert or breakfast since come to find out, there are no breakfast police.

Didn't have unsweetened chocolate squares so used a 2.4 oz dark chocolate candy bar instead. Reduced sugar to 1.5 cups. Upped zucchini to 3 cups. Criscoed and floured bread pans. Loaves popped right out, texture rich, moist, cakey, and most importantly, not too sweet. Couldn't be better!

Absolutely delicious! We found it to be even more tasty cold versus warm. I made the following changes... 6 tablespoons cocoa powder with 2 tablespoons oil and I increased zucchini to 2.5 cups packed.
